messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: Elevated 5xx on /v1/chat (us-east-1) — rolling 10m error rate 9.6% (baseline 0.3%). Source hint: model-serving-runtime crashes. Paging oncall.

kai: Im awake, looking at traces. Setting severity to sev2. @lin can you join live?

lin: on it. Grafana: errors correlate to route /v1/chat -> model redwood/nebula-13b:alpha. CPU fine but GPU runners show abrupt exits.

jorge: grabbing runner logs now:
```
kubectl -n inference logs -l app=model-runner -c runner --tail=400 | egrep -i "segfault|OOM|cudaMalloc|fatal|panic"
```

jorge: snippet:
```
[2026-03-16T03:12:22Z] runner[pid=44211] FATAL: Unexpected SIGSEGV at 0x7fff5c1a
[2026-03-16T03:12:22Z] runner[pid=44211] WARN: gpu_rss=52.3GB allocation failure
[2026-03-16T03:12:23Z] model-serving: returned 5xx: runtime crash
```

kai: any recent runtime/kernels pushed? lin?

lin: yes  memory-optimizer v1.1.0 pushed to canary at 00:45 PT, roughly 30% traffic. Telemetry indicates p95/p99 memory climbed for that variant.

jorge: further logs show a pattern: big multi-turn contexts + batched fanout. Example trace:
```
[2026-03-16T03:11:59Z] infer: req=pg-11, multi_turn=12, total_tokens=18000
[2026-03-16T03:12:05Z] kvcache: reserve 9.2GB
[2026-03-16T03:12:06Z] attention: reserve 31.7GB
[2026-03-16T03:12:22Z] cudaMalloc returned NULL
[2026-03-16T03:12:22Z] SIGSEGV at 0x0
```

kai: hypothesis: v1.1.0's new cache compaction interacts poorly with multi-turn batched requests creating a leak/overshoot. Plan: 1) divert traffic off alpha variant; 2) gate request size at gateway; 3) scale pool if needed; 4) rollback canary if necessary.

ops-bot: runbook pointer: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/runtime-oom. Suggested remediation: set routing to stable variant. Command:
```
redwoodctl routing override --path /v1/chat --model redwood/nebula-13b:stable --force
```

kai: applying routing override now.

kai: routing update applied. traffic -> stable in ~10s.

jorge: after shift, crash rate dropped ~68%. p50 latencies normal; p99 still skewed at ~3.4s.

lin: I've asked infra to add 3 extra GPU nodes to the us-east-1 pool while we validate. Request submitted, ETA ~3m.

jorge: infra added +3; runner pods rebalanced. Good.

sre: customer impact: two enterprise customers flagged errors: Parcelly and BlueCart. tagging and notifying CS.

cs-rep: Parcelly engineering reached out; they saw elevated failures from 03:10-03:18 UTC and several aborted flows. They want a short summary and time window.

jorge: digging logs for Parcelly request ids. Found multiple requests with long aggregated context due to their session-preserve setting. Example:
```
[2026-03-16T03:11:45Z] infer: req=pl-900, session_tokens=16400, batch=1
[2026-03-16T03:11:50Z] kvcache: allocate 12.1GB
[2026-03-16T03:11:51Z] attention: allocate 35.6GB
[2026-03-16T03:12:22Z] cudaMalloc failed
```

lin: Gateway-level mitigation: add a temporary transform to clip session context to last 8k tokens and mark request with header x-context-trimmed. Prefer clip over outright rejection to reduce customer errors.

jorge: deploying transform. snippet:
```
if (meta.tokens > 8192) { request.context = trim_to_last_n_tokens(request.context, 8192); request.headers['x-context-trimmed']='true'; }
```

jorge: transform deployed. downstream we see trimmed requests and 4xx for oversized payloads reduced; importantly, 5xx drops significantly.

sre: root cause note for ticket: memory-optimizer v1.1.0 compaction path increases transient allocation for multi-turn batched contexts causing GPU oversubscription and SIGSEGV. Secondary trigger: customer session-preserve enabling very long contexts.

kai: should we rollback v1.1.0 from canary to eliminate risk? Lin?

lin: yes, rollback is the quickest to remove regression. We'll block v1.1.0 until we can run targeted allocation tests and memory safety fixes. Jorge, can you issue rollback?

jorge: running rollback:
```
releasectl rollback memory-optimizer-v1.1.0 --target canary
```

jorge: rollback finished. canary now at v1.0.9. Observing 5xx rate back to baseline ~0.4% within 6m.

ops-bot: timeline note added: rollback completed 03:28 UTC.

cs-rep: Parcelly confirms errors stopped after ~03:18 UTC window and appreciates the update; asking for an incident update and SLA credit estimate.

sre: impact summary for post-incident: ~8 minutes of elevated 5xx affecting canary-routed customers; Parcelly and BlueCart had visible errors. Root cause: memory regression in memory-optimizer v1.1.0 under heavy multi-turn contexts.

kai: actions completed: traffic reroute, gateway clip guard, pool scale-up, rollback. Next actions: runtime team to reproduce with synthetic multi-turn loads (>=16k tokens), add unit/regression tests for cache compaction, and add a policy to block kernel rollouts that increase p99 memory by >10%.

lin: I'll own the runtime bug and the test harness. Jorge, can you upload allocation traces to INC-20260316-09 and assign to runtime-team?

jorge: uploaded logs, traces, and commands. Created bug RUNTIME-4938, assigned to runtime-team. Added synthetic test plan to run nightly.

kai: handoff: I need to step away. Jorge, can you take oncall for next 4 hours? I'll stay looped as incident lead for postmortem.

jorge: I can take the handoff. I'll keep monitoring until 07:30 UTC and run the synthetic 16k token run against a staging canary to ensure no regressions slip through.

ops-bot: pager downgraded to sev3 at 03:35 UTC and closed. Please update runbook with the new gating rule.

lin: quick synthetic result summary: v1.0.9 peak mem at 16k tokens ~45GB; v1.1.0 telemetry suggests ~67GB peak. Confirms ~+20GB regression.

sre: drafting incident impact note for postmortem. Mia or CS to prepare customer-facing summary.

kai: thanks team. Ticket INC-20260316-09 updated with timeline, rollback, and customer impact. Handing primary oncall to jorge at 03:40 UTC.

incident-bot: UPDATE: spike mitigated; rollback and gateway-trim applied; customer impact recorded. Incident INC-20260316-09."
